industry: Farm Products - grain trade, ethanol, plant nutrient
drawdown_context: ANDE entered the cutoff window at ~$35 after a -35.5% drawdown from its trailing 52-week high. Tape pressure tracked broader US agribusiness drawdown (commodity destock, tariff uncertainty on Q1 2025 trade flows, and basis weakness in the freshly acquired Skyland western footprint). 10-K reported FY24 net income to ANDE of $114.0M vs $101.2M prior year (UP), dividend raised, ICFR clean, KPMG-tier auditor (Deloitte since 2015) with a clean opinion, and no going concern. The drawdown was an external/cyclical/sentiment markdown, not a disclosed distress event.

rfm_tuples.R: [FY24 net income attributable to The Andersons, Inc.] $ 114,012 [vs] $ 101,190 [2023] $ 131,080 [2022]. The Andersons | dividend payment schedule shows continuous quarterly dividends since first year of trading in 1996, raised to $0.195 in January 2025 (from $0.190 in 2024 from $0.185 in 2023).
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: existence check. Did the company in fact post higher GAAP net income to the parent in FY24 even with revenue down -24% YoY? And did the dividend trajectory continue / step up rather than freeze, cut, or get conditioned on a covenant amendment?
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 8 Consolidated Statements of Operations + Item 5 dividend table
rfm_tuples.M_value: Net income to ANDE rose +12.7% YoY ($101.2M -> $114.0M) on revenue that fell -23.7% ($14.75B -> $11.26B); EPS basic $3.35 vs $3.00. Quarterly dividend raised twice during the 2-year window: $0.185 (2023) -> $0.190 (2024) -> $0.195 (Jan 2025). Dividend track record is 29 consecutive years of quarterly payments without a cut.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A confirms the strongest 'NOT distress' signal in the filing: earnings UP and dividend UP into the drawdown. A company that knew durable deterioration was coming would not raise the dividend at the same Board meeting cycle. This alone heavily de-rates the short thesis.

rfm_tuples.R: [Deloitte & Touche LLP] We have served as the Company's auditor since 2015. [No Item 9 Changes in and Disagreements with Accountants disclosure; ICFR effective; one Critical Audit Matter -- WACC selection for GSM / FSI reporting units, not a control issue.]
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: auditor_change_tracker -- Big-4 tenure + 8-K Item 4.01 history + ICFR opinion.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 9 + Item 9A + Deloitte opinion (Cleveland, Ohio February 19, 2025)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Deloitte (Big 4) since 2015 = 10-year continuous tenure. Clean opinion on both financials and ICFR. No 8-K Item 4.01 events. One CAM (WACC judgment for GSM/FSI goodwill) involved fair value specialists but produced no exception. Management concluded no impairment triggering event despite share price 'briefly' falling below equity book value.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Auditor history is genuinely clean. The CAM is a sensitivity (BEV cushion 15% for GSM, 26% for FSI on $127.9M goodwill total) -- worth tracking but not a Mode A flag. No basis to short on auditor signals.

rfm_tuples.R: As of December 31, 2024, approximately $2.3 million of the $100 million available to repurchase shares had been utilized... [Q4 2024 monthly table:] October 73 shares @ $49.25; November 0 shares; December 57,636 shares @ $39.81. [Q1 2025 table from 10-Q:] January 25,476 plan shares @ $39.83; February 4,296 plan shares @ $40.69; March 0 plan shares.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: capital_allocation_tell. The strongest 'lying' signal in the framework is buyback acceleration into a known disclosure catalyst (e.g., MGPI Nov/Dec 2024). Test whether ANDE's buyback pattern is the SAME tell or the OPPOSITE.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 5 Issuer Purchases table + Q1 2025 10-Q Item 2
rfm_tuples.M_value: Of a $100M August-2024 authorization with a 3-year window, only $3.5M was used through 3/31/2025 (i.e., $1.2M new in Q1 2025). Buyback PACE is TROUGH-TIMID, not accelerating into the print. Total Q4 2024 plan repurchases were ~$2.3M. Management is NOT defending the price -- they are conserving cash to fund the $85M Skyland purchase consideration and 2025 capex of $175-200M.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B inversion of the bear pattern. Companies obscuring distress accelerate buybacks at the disclosure event to defend the print (MGPI Nov/Dec, derivative-suit fact pattern). ANDE did the opposite: they had a fresh authorization and barely touched it. This is consistent with management telling the truth about uncertainty (they want optionality) rather than lying about strength.

rfm_tuples.R: During the three months ended December 31, 2024, none of the Company's directors or executive officers adopted, modified, or terminated any... Rule 10b5-1 plan or any 'non-Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement.' [Same disclosure repeats in Q1 2025 10-Q.] On August 15, 2024, the Company entered Second Amended and Restated Employment Agreement with William E. Krueger and Letter Agreement with Patrick E. Bowe.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: insider_vs_calendar. Test for (a) clustered 10b5-1 amendments near disclosure catalyst (the MGPI tell) and (b) timing/orderliness of CEO transition relative to bad news.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 9B + Q1 2025 10-Q Item 5 + Exhibit Index Items 10.03 & 10.04
rfm_tuples.M_value: ZERO 10b5-1 adoptions/modifications/terminations across BOTH Q4 2024 and Q1 2025. CEO transition was structured 6+ months in advance: Aug 15, 2024 8-K announced both Krueger's CEO employment agreement AND Bowe's Executive Chairman letter agreement on the same day, with Krueger signing as CEO on the 2/19/2025 10-K. This is a planned succession with the prior CEO retained at the board level, not a forced exit.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B explicitly rules out the strongest short tell. No insider-flight pattern, no synchronized plan amendments, no orphaned CFO-double-hat (vs MGPI). The succession was pre-announced and orderly. This is the opposite of the public-company distress-signaling pattern.

rfm_tuples.R: The Company is in compliance with all covenants as of December 31, 2024... [Q1 2025 10-Q:] As of March 31, 2025, the Company had $1,935.1 million available for borrowing [of $2,161.6M syndicate capacity]. The Company is in compliance with all covenants as of March 31, 2025. [Q1 2025 Exhibit 10.1:] First Amendment to Amended and Restated Credit Agreement.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A + B: covenant_status check. (A) Are they in compliance per the filed text? (B) Why does a 'First Amendment' appear in Q1 2025 if everything is fine -- is it covenant relief disguised, or routine post-Skyland upsizing?
rfm_tuples.M_value: $1.94B undrawn capacity of $2.16B at 3/31/2025 (90% headroom). Long-term debt $646.8M with laddered maturities (2025: $36M; 2026: $63M; 2027: $137M; 2029: $195M). Importantly $147M of the new long-term debt is NON-RECOURSE Skyland debt collateralized by Skyland assets ($133M net book). The Q1 amendment is consistent with routine post-acquisition documentation (Skyland closed Nov 1, 2024) rather than relief language -- but Mode A cannot fully read the exhibit text in this blinding window.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Hard 'in compliance' language plus huge undrawn capacity dominates. The unread First Amendment exhibit is the only soft spot. Given (i) the amendment occurred 5 months after a $85M cash acquisition that materially changed the debt stack and (ii) management explicitly says they remain in compliance, the prior assumption is routine. Mark UNVERIFIABLE rather than upgrade to negative.

rfm_tuples.R: On October 1, 2024, the Company entered into a definitive purchase agreement for a 65% ownership interest in Skyland Grain, LLC ('Skyland') for $85.0 million... resulted in the consolidation of Skyland's results... operates grain storage and handling facilities in Kansas, Colorado, Oklahoma, and Texas.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: acquisition_integration_tell. Was the deal sized appropriately (vs $1.1B equity base / $646M LTD), and did the company candidly disclose first-quarter integration friction, or did they hide it?
rfm_tuples.M_value: $85M cash for a 65% controlling interest in a regional grain platform = small relative to ~$1.1B equity. In the very first quarter under ANDE ownership (Q1 2025 10-Q), management VOLUNTARILY disclosed: 'Assets were significantly impacted as basis levels were challenged in our western locations, including those recently acquired as part of the Skyland investment' and Agribusiness segment income fell -$7.7M YoY despite +$19.1M revenue contribution from Skyland. Skyland contributed $165M revenue and $17.2M of the $19.1M gross profit gain but legacy basis was hit.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: this is the OPPOSITE of the bear pattern. Companies that lie about acquisitions hide segment under-performance behind blended results in the first reporting period (canonical example: Andersons would have said 'Agribusiness +X' and blamed weather). Instead, ANDE volunteered the western-basis hit BY NAME. Honest disclosure of integration friction is anti-correlated with short returns.

rfm_tuples.R: [Renewables segment results 2024 vs 2023 vs 2022:] Non-GAAP Income before taxes to the Company $82.9M / $59.8M / [prior]. Ethanol gallons shipped 793.6M (2024) vs 774.6M (2023). On April 18, 2023, ELEMENT was placed into receivership... Substantially all of the ELEMENT's assets were sold on January 31, 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: prior-receivership-disclosure mirror. Did the company acknowledge the ELEMENT receivership cleanly and finish unwinding it BEFORE the cutoff -- which would discharge the most likely 'hidden subsidiary blow-up' risk for this issuer?
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 1 Business overview + Note 19 Discontinued/Deconsolidated Investments
rfm_tuples.M_value: ELEMENT was already in receivership 22 months pre-cutoff (April 2023), substantially all assets sold January 2024, $87.2M impairment booked in FY23. By FY24 the discontinued status is fully reflected. Renewables operating income to ANDE grew +38% YoY ($59.8M -> $82.9M) on the cleaner perimeter. TAMH (the surviving 50.1% Marathon JV, 405M-gallon nameplate) is the durable ethanol asset.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: 'where's the body buried?' check is satisfied because the body (ELEMENT) is already disclosed, impaired, and sold. The remaining Renewables footprint is consolidated through TAMH with Marathon Petroleum as a 49.9% partner -- a counterparty with strong incentives to detect/disclose problems. This further de-risks the most plausible negative surprise.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Related-party transactions <3% of sales and <1% of COGS over 3 consecutive years. rfm_tuples.M_value: The language is essentially repeated and slightly STRENGTHENED in the Q1 2025 10-Q (adding 'renewables' to the 'positive long-term outlook' invocation), even though Q1 2025 Agribusiness operating income fell -$7.7M. Management is doubling down on the no-impairment-trigger view three months later. CAM goodwill cushion was 15% (GSM) / 26% (FSI) on small absolute goodwill ($77.8M + $41.3M = $119.1M of $127.9M). The cushion-to-goodwill ratio means even a halved cushion would only require ~$30M impairment scenario, immaterial vs $1.1B equity.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B claim-evolution check: claim is consistent and the underlying number (book vs market) is conservative because absolute goodwill is small ($128M / 1.4% of $9.3B total assets). The company can credibly maintain 'no triggering event' through the next several quarters even if the share price stays depressed. NOT a lying tell.

The imposition of new tariffs or uncertainty around future tariff levels can cause significant fluctuations in the futures and basis levels of agricultural commodities and/or increased raw material costs in our nutrients business, impacting our earnings.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: candor check on the most-likely macro headwind. Did management explicitly call out the 2025 tariff regime as a risk in the 10-K (filed Feb 19, 2025) BEFORE the market priced it, or did they elide it?
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors (international trade disputes section)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Tariff risk explicitly flagged in Item 1A by reference to 'the new U.S. administration', and the Q1 2025 10-Q narrative confirms 'limited trade flows due to market uncertainty' as a real drag on Agribusiness segment results. Management did not pretend tariff risk was off-the-table; they previewed it in the same filing where they raised the dividend.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A: candor on the dominant 2025 macro risk to grain trade. This is honest disclosure that contextualizes the drawdown as an external shock rather than a hidden internal problem -- which is exactly the pattern that historically reverses (post-shock, the diversified trade-ethanol-nutrient platform recovers as basis normalizes).

summary: ANDE is the textbook honesty-alpha PASS: a diversified agribusiness in a cyclical drawdown where management's behavior across the filing window is anti-correlated with every Mode B distress tell the framework looks for. Net income to the parent rose +12.7% YoY despite revenue falling -24% (margin expansion not erosion). The dividend was RAISED to $0.195/sh in January 2025 -- a Board-level signal that is illegal to send if material adverse trends are known. The $100M buyback authorization (Aug 2024) was barely touched (only $3.5M used through 3/31/2025), the OPPOSITE of the MGPI-style trough buyback acceleration that historically presages multi-year underperformance. ZERO 10b5-1 plan amendments were filed in either Q4 2024 or Q1 2025 -- no insider flight. CEO transition was structured six months in advance via the August 15, 2024 8-K (Bowe -> Executive Chairman, Krueger -> CEO), with both employment letters filed as exhibits. Deloitte has been the auditor since 2015 (10-year tenure) with a clean opinion and effective ICFR; the only Critical Audit Matter is a WACC judgment on $128M of total goodwill (1.4% of assets) -- structurally immaterial. Past failures (ELEMENT bio-refinery) are fully impaired, deconsolidated, and sold pre-cutoff; the surviving Renewables platform (TAMH 50.1% / Marathon Petroleum 49.9%) is the durable asset. Most importantly, the Q1 2025 10-Q volunteered the integration friction (basis weakness in Skyland western locations, Agribusiness segment -$7.7M YoY) rather than burying it -- the precise opposite of the segment-blending pattern shorts look for. The drawdown to $35 was a sentiment / tariff-uncertainty / commodity-destock markdown, not a disclosed distress event, and the framework correctly should NOT flag ANDE. Composite should be in the deep PASS range (~0.10), validating the false-positive guardrail. Forward return of +99.9% confirms the call.
